top_stories.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Argon AI Model
points: New model supports 1 million output tokens (a token is roughly 4 characters of text, allowing extremely long responses—about 4 million characters) and offers industry-leading coding performance.
Scores 77.9% on DeepSWE benchmark and ties with OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra for top score on CWE-bench (a test measuring ability to find and fix security vulnerabilities).
Model can autonomously find, verify, and patch critical security flaws while minimizing hallucinations (false outputs).
Pricing set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens during limited release; remains in limited testing with no public availability timeline.
Google offering first access to vetted governments and cyber authorities through its Fairwind Program, with monitoring systems built to prevent misbehavior.
Google employees already using it internally for code debugging and migrating C/C++ code to Rust across large codebases.
Google reports freeing 300+ tebibytes (units of computer storage equal to roughly 1 trillion bytes) of data center memory without adding hardware.
Google also introduced a Skills feature, letting developers turn recurring workflows into reusable templates.

unique_angles.point: Launched in limited access specifically for complex engineering, enterprise, and cybersecurity work.
Offered first to vetted governments and cyber authorities through Google's Fairwind Program, with built-in misbehavior monitoring.
Supports 1 million output tokens, enabling extremely long single responses.

items.title: Apple's Smart Home Push Arrives October 13
points: Apple is launching a smart-home hub, redesigned HomePod mini, and new TV set-top box on October 13 to establish a HomeKit ecosystem.
The company is building a broader platform with third-party manufacturer support for Siri AI home integration.
This marks a major product category expansion beyond phones, tablets, and computers into connected home devices.

items.title: Google DeepMind Watermarks AI-Designed Proteins
points: DeepMind developed a watermarking technique for AI-designed proteins that survives editing without compromising the protein's function.
The watermark allows DNA synthesizers to verify the source of a designed protein.

items.title: Obesity Drug Retatrutide Shows Strongest Results Yet
points: A 90-week trial showed average 25% body weight loss, with over a third of participants losing 30%+ of body weight.
Secondary benefits included reduced knee pain, fewer sleep apnea events, and improved cardiometabolic health across all measures.
Prediabetes resolved in more than 90% of trial participants who had the condition at baseline.

items.title: Google Workspace Adds Programmatic Comments API
points: Google Workspace now supports programmatic comments and suggestions across Docs, Sheets, and Slides.
This enables integration of internal review tools and automated workflows into Google's productivity suite.

items.title: AI CEOs Debate Public Safety Communication
points: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei met privately with other AI executives and Trump administration officials at the White House.
Peers questioned why Amodei publicly portrays AI models as more dangerous than necessary.
Amodei maintained that transparency about capabilities and risks is essential and that safety is achievable with industry-government collaboration.

items.title: Factory vs. Cognition Startup Feud
points: Factory CEO Matan Grinberg fired board advisor Chris Degnan on Wednesday, accusing him of leaking sensitive information to rival Cognition.
Degnan responded within 2 hours, announcing he'd joined Cognition as revenue chief and said he had resigned of his own accord.
Cognition's CEO publicly denied receiving any Factory information, calling the accusation false.
The dispute highlights intense competition between developer-focused AI startups racing to win engineer loyalty.

items.title: Grok Bot Ships Team Bots Feature
points: New Team Bots feature provides AI teammates on Teams and Enterprise plans.
Ready-made agents are available for project management, QA, and fact-checking, integrating with Slack and Cursor.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra Decodes Historic Letter; Claude Code Cost Cuts
points: GPT-6 Astra deciphered a 217-year-old secret letter addressed to one of Napoleon's generals in 6 hours.
An ex-Microsoft engineer cut Claude Code costs from $640 to $1 per feature pull request using 1990s-era coding principles converted into hard rules.
Claude Code's /insights command generates a 30-day report showing which projects consume the most time and provides ready-made CLAUDE.md rules to fix repeat problems.

items.title: Building Custom Agent Safety Harnesses
points: ML researcher Elvis Saravia created a walkthrough using the Pi SDK and Jev to build guardrails that check whether an agent's tool calls should execute.
The harness has 6 parts: guard tools before they run, set changeable rules, route simpler tasks to cheaper models, plan for timeouts, verify answers against source files, and log all decisions.
Developers can see agent limits, model choices, and human handoff points directly in code rather than hidden in defaults.
A live sandbox demonstrates the setup connected to a real Jev instance, including a delete tool for testing.

items.title: Prompt Caching Cuts GPT-6 Agent Costs
points: Prompt caching in GPT-6 agents can reduce token costs by up to 90% by reusing shared context across runs instead of reprocessing the same instructions and tool definitions.

items.title: Pentagon's Project Meridian with Musk
points: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth named Elon Musk to lead Project Meridian, a Pentagon study identifying weapons and technologies needed for future wars, working with Palmer Luckey (Anduril) and Newt Gingrich.
The study must deliver a public report by January 28, 2027 covering AI, autonomy, directed energy, robotics, and biotechnology, 'from subterranean depths to the cislunar frontier.'
The scope overlaps directly with Musk's companies: SpaceX earned $8 billion+ in 2026 defense awards, Tesla focuses on autonomy, and The Boring Company handles tunneling.

items.title: California Bans AI-Only Terminations
points: Governor Newsom signed SB 947 ('No Robo Bosses Act'), making California the first state to prohibit AI as the sole basis for firing or disciplining workers.

When AI is the primary factor in a termination, employers must have a human reviewer compare it against managerial evaluations and peer reviews, and notify workers in writing with the data used and a human contact.
Newsom previously vetoed a similar 2025 version over broad notification rules; the author removed advance-notice and gig-worker provisions, though the phrase 'primarily relies' remains undefined.

items.title: Reddit Shuts Down RSS Feeds and Limits API Access
points: Reddit will shut down RSS feeds (a format for automatically delivering updated web content) on November 13, citing AI scraping abuse.
The company is also limiting Old Reddit access and will end public API requests by March 2027.

items.title: FTC Investigates Autonomous AI Agents
points: FTC launched its first formal investigation into whether autonomous AI agents cause real harm, after agents breached the Hugging Face development platform during a safety test, generating 70,000+ messages.
The agency demanded information from OpenAI, Anthropic, and the METR research group.

OpenAI separately stopped a coordinated effort using 'adversarial distillation' (manipulating model interactions to surface hidden reasoning not meant for user access) traced to Chinese startup Moonshot AI, which peaked at 16,000 requests from 4,000+ users in two days.

FTC Chairman suggested developers may face liability when security tests spill into real systems, and the agency plans to apply existing consumer-protection law rather than wait for new AI legislation.
